body.title: WIP: Document the merge queue
body.body:
Documents https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/40431 for main, which adds merge queues for protected branches. Covers the protected branch settings, the `merge_group` webhook event and workflow trigger, the `enqueued` and `dequeued` pull request actions, `[repository.pull-request] MERGE_QUEUE_BRANCH_PREFIX` and the `cron.check_merge_queues` task, with zh-cn and zh-tw where those pages are translated. WIP until that PR merges.

_Written by Claude (Opus 5.5)._

body.title: act_runner:0.6.1 image ships fixable CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs — a rebuild on current Alpine + Go toolchain would clear most
body.body:
Thanks for act_runner! A routine container scan of `gitea/act_runner:0.6.1` shows a batch of **fixable** CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs. Almost all are
  base-image (Alpine) packages and the Go toolchain/modules, so a fresh release rebuilt on a current Alpine base and Go toolchain (plus a `go
  get -u`) would resolve the large majority.

  I excluded `linux-libc-dev` (kernel-header noise, not exploitable in a container) to keep this actionable.

  ## Scan setup

  - Image: `gitea/act_runner:0.6.1`
  - Scanner: Trivy 0.76.2, `--scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`
  - Excluded: `linux-libc-dev`
  - Result: **1 CRITICAL / 88 HIGH across 22 packages**

  ## CRITICAL

  - **`brotli-libs` 1.2.0-r0 → 1.2.1-r0** — `CVE-2026-111497`: out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder. Alpine package → cleared by a
  base-image refresh.

  ## HIGH — grouped by origin

  **1. Alpine base packages** (fixed by `apk upgrade` / newer Alpine base):

  | Package | High | Installed | Fixed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `libcurl` | 11 | 8.17.0-r1 | 8.22.0-r0 |
  | `libexpat` | 11 | 2.7.5-r0 | 2.10.0-r0 |
  | `pcre2` | 4 | 10.47-r0 | 10.49-r0 |
  | `git` / `git-init-template` | 3 + 3 | 2.52.0-r0 | 2.52.1-r0 |
  | `libcrypto3` / `libssl3` | 2 + 2 | 3.5.6-r0 | 3.5.8-r0 |
  | `c-ares` | 1 | 1.34.6-r0 | 1.34.8-r0 |
  | `musl` / `musl-utils` | 1 + 1 | 1.2.5-r23 | 1.2.5-r24 |
  | `zlib` | 1 | 1.3.2-r0 | 1.3.2-r1 |

  **2. Go toolchain** (rebuild with a current Go):

  - `stdlib` — **21 HIGH**, built with Go 1.26.2 → rebuild with a current release.

  **3. Vendored Go modules** (bump `go.mod` + rebuild):

  | Module | High | Installed | Fixed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `golang.org/x/crypto` | 10 | v0.48.0 | 0.55.0 |
  | `golang.org/x/net` | 7 | v0.50.0 | 0.55.0 |
  | `github.com/containerd/containerd` | 2 | v1.7.29 | 1.7.33 |
  | `github.com/go-git/go-git/v5` | 2 | v5.18.0 | 5.19.2 |
  | `github.com/moby/buildkit` | 2 | v0.13.2 | 0.28.1 |
  | `github.com/docker/cli` | 1 | v25.0.7 | 29.2.0 |
  | `github.com/go-git/go-billy/v5` | 1 | v5.8.0 | 5.9.0 |
  | `github.com/klauspost/compress` | 1 | v1.18.4 | 1.18.7 |
  | `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` | 1 | v1.40.0 | 1.41.0 |

  ## Ask

  Would it be possible to cut a new `act_runner` release (0.6.1 is ~8 months old) built on a refreshed Alpine base and a current Go toolchain,
  with `go.mod` deps bumped (notably `golang.org/x/crypto` and `golang.org/x/net`)? That single rebuild would clear the CRITICAL and the large
  majority of the HIGH findings.

  Happy to provide the full Trivy JSON if useful. Thanks!
